title: Viv's ChatGPT sales jumped 436% | GEO
description: Period care brand Viv saw sales from ChatGPT recommendations jump 436%. Here is what it had published that AI tools picked up.
h1: Viv saw sales from ChatGPT recommendations jump 436%
intro: Period care brand Viv told Modern Retail that many shoppers sent to its blog by ChatGPT went on to buy, and sales from those recommendations jumped 436%. The brand also credits Google's AI recommendations for selling out about six months of tampon stock in three weeks.

keyNumbers.label: jump in sales converted from ChatGPT recommendations
spike in monthly traffic in July 2024, driven mainly by Gemini and ChatGPT
to sell out about six months of tampon stock

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: In July 2024 Viv's monthly traffic spiked by 400%. Marketing and design director Kelly Donohue said it came out of nowhere. When she dug in, she found most of it came from Google Gemini and ChatGPT recommending non-toxic period care.

The timing mattered. A study in the journal Environment International had just reported heavy metals such as lead and arsenic in many popular tampon brands. People were asking AI assistants about toxins in tampons, and the answers pointed them to Viv's blog. Many of those visitors bought.

sections.heading: What Viv had published
paragraphs: Right after the study came out, Viv posted an article titled "Lead & Arsenic in Tampons?! Here's Why Viv is Your Safest Tampon Choice." Donohue said it was the brand's top converting post of 2024.

Viv's website and social posts go into fine detail about how its products are made, ingredient safety and product testing. The brand also put its safety standards at the centre of its email, SMS and social media. Donohue believes having information about the brand in as many places as possible helped AI tools pick it up.

sections.heading: The Google side
paragraphs: The effect carried on in the months that followed. Donohue credits Google's AI-powered recommendations for a sell-out of tampon stock that was meant to last about six months.

quotes.text: We ended up selling out of about six months of tampon inventory in three weeks, driven by Google's AI-powered recommendations.
quotes.who: Kelly Donohue, marketing and design director at Viv

quotes.text: These AI tools are specifically scraping through content, but looking for more than just keywords.
quotes.who: Kelly Donohue, marketing and design director at Viv

lessons: Answer the question people are asking right now. Viv's article on lead and arsenic in tampons went up as soon as the study made news, and it became the brand's top converting post of 2024.
Go into detail. Viv explains manufacturing, ingredient safety and testing, the kind of context Donohue says AI tools look for when they build an answer.
Say the same thing everywhere. Viv carried its safety message across its blog, email, SMS and social media.
caveat: The 436% figure is Modern Retail's summary of Viv's results. The article does not give the sales figure it grew from.

source.title: Brands are seeing an influx of traffic from ChatGPT and Google Gemini
source.author: Gabriela Barkho

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: Draco Diamond sells made-to-order lab-grown diamond jewellery online. In spring 2026, founder Garrett McMartin focused on getting the brand to show up in AI answers. Afterwards, AI tools made up 5.45% of the site's traffic, up from 0.18% before. In May and July, AI's share of sessions reached 7.3% and 6.6%.

lessons: Measure AI as its own channel. McMartin tracked AI's share of sessions month by month, which is how he could see it move from 0.18% to 5.45%.

Look past traffic. AI visitors were Draco's highest-intent group, adding to cart five times as often as Google Ads visitors.
caveat: The revenue growth is a correlation the founder noticed, as the article says. It does not prove the AI work caused it.

intro: Founder Nishit Mehta told Digital Commerce 360 that shoppers who reach La Joya Jewelry through AI tools convert at more than 13%, where the store's normal rate is 3%. AI's share of its referral traffic grew from about 2% to 3% at the start of 2026 to about 5% or 6%.

sections.heading: The numbers
paragraphs: La Joya Jewelry sells lab-grown diamonds online. At the start of 2026, about 2% to 3% of its referral traffic came from AI sources. By early September it was about 5% or 6%.

Mehta said conversion rates for these visitors are double digits higher. As an example, he said that if the store's conversion rate is normally 3%, it rises to more than 13% for shoppers arriving through AI.

paragraphs: Mehta's view is that a recommendation carries trust. A shopper who has been told a company is good is more likely to believe it. He also said the biggest trend is that these shoppers have already done their research.

AI shoppers arrive informed. La Joya's visitors from AI have usually done their research, so they need less convincing on the basics.

h1: One ChatGPT question brought Hingees an order of over ₦250,000
intro: Nigerian lifestyle brand Hingees received a first-time order of over ₦250,000 from a shopper who had asked ChatGPT for Nigerian leather brands, TechCabal reported. It is one order, not a trend, but it surprised the founder.

keyNumbers.label: spent by one first-time buyer who found Hingees through ChatGPT

sections.heading: The order
paragraphs: Hingees sells leather goods and clothing. First-time buyers usually start small, with a shirt or maybe a notebook. So when a new customer placed a leather goods order of over ₦250,000, it looked like it might be fraud, and someone from the team called to confirm.

sections.heading: The groundwork behind it
paragraphs: Founder Hammed Okunade describes Hingees as obsessive about clean metadata, tagged photos and smart keywords, work it did for years to show up in Google. TechCabal's point is that AI assistants now squeeze research, comparison and the decision into one conversation, and that groundwork is what they can read.

The article argues that a small brand with good product data and images can appear next to bigger brands without paying for ads, while sellers who only use Instagram or WhatsApp risk being invisible to AI tools.

quotes.text: I always thought large orders came from returning customers or ads, and they still do. I just never imagined a chatbot would also be bringing us customers.

lessons: Clean product details keep paying off. Okunade spent years on tidy metadata, tagged photos and keywords, the kind of information TechCabal says AI tools can read.
Small brands can appear next to big ones. TechCabal argues good product data and images can get a small store recommended without paying for ads.
Find out how new buyers found you. Hingees only learned about ChatGPT because the customer mentioned it on the confirmation call.
caveat: This is a single order. It shows what can happen, not what usually happens.

title: SteelSeries: AI search revenue grew 3.7X | GEO
description: Gaming brand SteelSeries and its agency report traffic from AI search up 23X and revenue from AI search platforms up 3.7X.
h1: SteelSeries grew revenue from AI search platforms 3.7X
intro: Gaming gear brand SteelSeries and its agency, NoGood, report that over a ten-month program, traffic from AI search platforms grew 23X year over year, conversions from that traffic grew 27X and revenue from AI search platforms grew 3.7X. The figures come from an award-winning case study published by The Drum.

keyNumbers.label: year-over-year growth in traffic from AI search platforms
growth in conversions from those visitors
growth in revenue from AI search platforms

sections.heading: What they found first
paragraphs: Early research showed that AI recommendations for gaming hardware were shaped by a surprisingly small number of sources: a handful of review publications and a cluster of Reddit threads. So getting recommended meant earning coverage and community trust, not just improving SteelSeries' own site.

sections.heading: What they changed
paragraphs: Product pages were rebuilt with short answers near the top, question and answer sections and simple tables that AI tools can quote. Structured data was added across the site, and rendering problems that were stopping crawlers from reading pages were fixed.

Outreach went to the specific publishers and reviewers shaping AI answers in the category, and stale coverage was replaced with current mentions. On Reddit, the team joined the exact threads AI was citing with genuinely useful posts rather than promotion. Product feeds were also prepared for ChatGPT Shopping, Amazon Rufus and Google AI Mode shopping.

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: Traffic from AI search platforms grew 23X year over year, reaching more than 1,500 daily visitors by October 2025. Conversions from those visitors grew 27X, with conversion rates that beat traditional search, and revenue from AI search platforms grew 3.7X. By the end, SteelSeries held the top spot for gaming headsets, keyboards and earbuds on Gemini, ChatGPT and Perplexity.

lessons: Find the sources AI trusts in your category. For SteelSeries it was a few review sites and Reddit threads, so that is where the effort went.
Make product pages easy to quote. Short answers up top, question and answer sections and clear tables give AI tools clean text to use.
Check nothing is blocking crawlers. Fixing pages that crawlers could not read was part of the work.
Join conversations honestly. The team added useful posts to the Reddit threads AI cited, not brand promotion.
caveat: These numbers come from the agency's award entry, not independent reporting. NoGood's own case study page gives different figures in its body text (6.7X traffic growth and a 7.1X rise in conversions), so treat them with care.

h1: Levenger's sales from ChatGPT went from $790 to $20,500
intro: Premium stationery retailer Levenger made $790 from ChatGPT referrals in all of 2024 and $20,500 in 2025 up to the time of the report, according to a case study by its agency, Volume Nine. The agency also reports $92 of value per AI visitor, against a $6 site average.

keyNumbers.label: total sales from ChatGPT referrals in all of 2024

sections.heading: Where Levenger started
paragraphs: Levenger sells notebooks, pens and workspace products to writers, readers and professionals. Organic search had long brought in customers, but it was becoming less predictable as traffic fell and competition grew. More buyers were doing their research inside AI tools instead.
In 2024, ChatGPT referrals brought in just $790 in total sales. AI search existed for the brand, but it was not a reliable source of customers.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The agency worked on three things: technical changes so AI tools could crawl the site and cite it accurately, clearer product education content, and more visibility off the site through social media and editorial coverage. Every decision was tested against one question: if a buyer asked ChatGPT for recommendations for serious writers or professionals, would Levenger show up?

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: For 2025 year to date, the agency reports $20,500 in sales directly from ChatGPT, a 2,275% increase in AI-driven revenue year over year, and $92 of value per AI visitor against a $6 site-wide average. It says visitors from ChatGPT were more informed and more likely to convert than visitors from other channels.

lessons: Teach before you sell. Levenger's work focused on clear product education, because premium buyers want context before they spend.
Picture the exact question. The work was judged by whether Levenger would come up when someone asked ChatGPT for products for serious writers.
Value per visitor matters more than volume. A small number of AI visitors can count when each is worth $92 against a $6 average.
caveat: This is the agency's own case study and no one at Levenger is quoted. The same page shows lower figures in its summary boxes ($7,841 in ChatGPT sales, an 871% increase and $35 per AI visitor) without explaining the difference.

title: Ahrefs: 12.1% of sign-ups from AI search | GEO
description: At Ahrefs, visitors from AI search were 0.5% of traffic but brought 12.1% of sign-ups, converting 23 times better than Google visitors.
h1: At Ahrefs, 0.5% of visitors brought 12.1% of sign-ups
intro: Marketing software company Ahrefs found that visitors from AI search made up just 0.5% of its traffic over 30 days, but brought 12.1% of its sign-ups. On its numbers, AI search visitors converted 23 times better than visitors from traditional organic search.

keyNumbers.label: of Ahrefs' traffic came from AI search over the last 30 days
of sign-ups came from AI search in the same period
better conversion than visitors from traditional organic search

sections.heading: What Ahrefs measured
paragraphs: Patrick Stox looked at Ahrefs' own website data. He counted AI search as visits from assistants like ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini. Over the last 30 days they made up 0.5% of traffic, and 0.3% for the year to date. Most of that traffic came from ChatGPT, and so did the vast majority of the sign-ups.
Even so, those visitors produced 12.1% of all sign-ups, making AI search Ahrefs' channel with the highest conversions per visit.

sections.heading: Not all good news
paragraphs: Other measures were mixed. Fewer AI visitors left straight away and they viewed 50% more pages, but they spent less time on the site. Stox also estimated, from rough modelling, that people in AI search click links 75% less than in traditional search, and he was not sure the higher conversion rate would scale up enough to make up for it.

quotes.text: That's crazy right? 12.1% of signups from 0.5% of the traffic. This channel performs really well for us.
quotes.who: Patrick Stox, Technical SEO at Ahrefs when he wrote the post

lessons: Judge AI by results, not visits. A tiny slice of traffic produced an outsized share of sign-ups.
Check where AI visitors land. Ahrefs found most went to its home page, free tools and product pages, so those pages need to be ready.
Expect fewer clicks overall. If people click less in AI answers, each visit you do get counts for more.
caveat: This is one software company's 30-day snapshot. Ahrefs sells subscriptions, not products, and sign-ups are not sales.

source.title: Does AI Search Traffic Convert Better Than Traditional Search? For Ahrefs, Yes: 0.5% of Visitors Drove 12.1% of Signups

description: Webflow gets 10% of sign-ups from AI tools, up 4x in a year, and ChatGPT visitors convert at 24%. What its growth team learned.
h1: Webflow now gets 10% of its sign-ups from AI tools
intro: Website builder Webflow gets 10% of its sign-ups from AI discovery, up 4x year on year, according to figures from its VP of Growth, Josh Grant, in Kyle Poyar's Growth Unhinged newsletter. Visitors from ChatGPT convert at 24%, six times the rate of Google.

keyNumbers.label: of Webflow's sign-ups come from AI discovery, up 4x year on year
conversion rate for traffic from ChatGPT, 6x higher than Google
of Webflow's AI referrals come from ChatGPT alone

sections.heading: The numbers
paragraphs: Webflow is a website building company with about 300,000 customers. 10% of its sign-ups now come from AI tools, up 4x in a year, and the newsletter notes this tracked figure likely understates the full effect.

91% of those AI referrals come from ChatGPT, followed by Perplexity (4%), Copilot (2%), Gemini (2%) and Claude (1%). ChatGPT traffic converts at 24%, six times Google's rate, and two in three AI-referred conversions happen within seven days.

sections.heading: What Webflow learned
paragraphs: Total traffic can mislead: Webflow's lower-value visits fell while higher-quality visits grew. AI answers also change constantly, so showing up one day does not guarantee showing up the next.

The team tracks three things: how often Webflow appears in AI answers, how accurately AI tools describe it compared with competitors, and how many sign-ups come from AI. It tried an llms.txt file and saw no significant lift. And it treats Reddit as an important signal, answering real questions there instead of dropping links.

quotes.text: A lot of our lower value and lower intent traffic has gone down, but there's higher quality traffic occurring even as the aggregate declines.
quotes.who: Josh Grant, VP of Growth at Webflow

quotes.text: When I say AI engines are volatile, I mean it's not like Google where you rank once and hold it.
quotes.who: Josh Grant, VP of Growth at Webflow

lessons: Don't judge by total traffic. Webflow's weaker visits fell while better ones grew.
Check what AI says about you. Webflow compares how different AI assistants describe it against competitors and fixes what is wrong.
Skip the shortcuts. Webflow saw no significant lift from an llms.txt file and focuses on content instead.
Be useful on Reddit. Webflow answers the questions people actually ask rather than posting links.
caveat: Webflow sells software, not products, and sign-ups are not sales. The rest of the newsletter post is for paid subscribers.

source.author: Kyle Poyar

paragraphs: Vercel's post starts from a simple observation: AI tools now answer many questions directly, often without a single click. sections.heading: 2025: ChatGPT moves to the top
paragraphs: Tally has always grown through word of mouth and organic search. lessons: Be present where people talk. Tally credits years of honest answers and sharing in forums and on Reddit, which AI tools now read.

description: Adaptive clothing brand Joe & Bella saw new customers arrive from ChatGPT, and some bought over the holidays. What the brand thinks helped.
h1: ChatGPT sent Joe & Bella new customers who bought over the holidays
intro: Adaptive clothing brand Joe & Bella saw an influx of new customers arriving from ChatGPT, and a number of them bought during the 2024 holiday season, Modern Retail reported. The article gives no sales figures.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Joe & Bella sells clothing that makes dressing easier for older adults and people living with conditions such as Parkinson's. In the months before the article, the brand saw an influx of new customers coming to its website from ChatGPT, and a number of those visitors bought over the holidays.
Co-founder and CEO Jimmy Zollo admitted he did not know what those shoppers had asked ChatGPT to find the brand.

sections.heading: What the brand thinks helped
paragraphs: Zollo's theory is that the search keywords the brand keeps investing in, and its blog, are the likely reasons. Its search ads often use terms such as "adaptive clothing".
Joe & Bella planned to keep investing in content about its products' technology, along with related keywords that AI chatbots can pick up.

quotes.text: I don't really know how or what they would have typed or asked ChatGPT to have found us over the holidays.
quotes.who: Jimmy Zollo, co-founder and CEO of Joe & Bella

quotes.text: It was pretty cool and unexpected, but we need to better understand how to optimize for these searches going forward.
quotes.who: Jimmy Zollo, co-founder and CEO of Joe & Bella

lessons: Steady content work can surface in AI answers. Zollo believes the brand's ongoing keyword work and blog are why ChatGPT found it.
Explain what makes your products different. Joe & Bella planned more content about its products' technology for AI chatbots to pick up.
You may never see the question. Even the CEO did not know what shoppers typed into ChatGPT before they arrived.
caveat: The article gives no numbers. It shows that shoppers from ChatGPT bought, not how many or how much.

source.title: Brands are seeing an influx of traffic from ChatGPT and Google Gemini
source.author: Gabriela Barkho

cardHeadline: AI referrals up 2,434% over Black Friday and Cyber Monday
title: JBL: AI referrals up 2,434% at Black Friday | GEO
description: Audio brand JBL saw referrals from AI tools rise 2,434% over Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025 after rethinking its content for AI.
h1: JBL's referrals from AI tools rose 2,434% over Black Friday
intro: Audio brand JBL, working with agency Code and Theory, saw referrals from AI tools rise 2,434% across Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025, according to data the two companies shared with Marketing Brew. The article reports visits, not sales.

keyNumbers.label: rise in referrals from AI tools over Black Friday and Cyber Monday
higher engagement on four search-tuned YouTube Shorts than JBL's 30-day average

sections.heading: What JBL changed
paragraphs: JBL worked with Code and Theory to audit its search practices, rethink its website and build an editorial plan that works for human readers and automated crawlers alike. The stories aim to be fun to read but also clear on features, and they tackle everyday doubts such as whether a soundbar is actually worth buying.

For Black Friday, JBL published a gift guide showing which of its products suit different kinds of gift recipients. The team also studied how people search on YouTube and TikTok, and made short videos to match, such as a YouTube Short comparing two speakers.

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: Across Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025, referrals from AI tools were up 2,434%. Four optimised YouTube Shorts reached a 2.61% engagement rate by view, which the agency says is 200x JBL's 30-day average of 0.013%.
The agency described the work as slow and steady rather than an overnight win, and JBL is still working out how to roll it out across regions.

quotes.text: We wanted to identify what was the best strategy for JBL, and not just a generic strategy for SEO.
quotes.who: Carolina González, manager, global digital content strategy at JBL

quotes.text: The way that we see it, search is everywhere now. But that doesn't mean that people search the same way on every platform.
quotes.who: Bryn Dodson, creative director, copy, at Code and Theory (JBL's agency)

lessons: Answer the doubts buyers have. JBL writes around everyday questions, like whether a soundbar is worth buying.
Let your gift guide do the matching. JBL's Black Friday guide said which products suit which kind of recipient.
Treat it as a long game. JBL's agency calls this slow and steady work, not overnight growth.
caveat: The press article confirms the jump in referrals only. JBL's award entry also claims "10x more revenue than the next highest period" but does not say what that revenue covers, so we don't count it as a sales result.

source.title: 'Search is everywhere': How JBL is retooling its search efforts for AI
source.author: Kristina Monllos

cardHeadline: Sales from AI referrals up 78%, mostly via ChatGPT
title: RAVE Coffee: AI-referred sales up 78% | GEO
description: An agency reports a 78% rise in sales attributed to AI referrals for UK roaster RAVE Coffee, with ChatGPT behind over 95% of them.
h1: RAVE Coffee's agency reports a 78% rise in AI-referred sales
intro: UK agency The SEO Works reports a 78% uplift in sales directly attributed to AI referrals for a coffee brand, shown on the case study by the RAVE Coffee logo. ChatGPT accounted for more than 95% of those AI-driven transactions.

keyNumbers.label: uplift in sales directly attributed to AI referrals
of AI-driven transactions came from ChatGPT
year-on-year rise in AI-assisted conversions

sections.heading: What the agency did
paragraphs: The SEO Works audited the content and mapped what shoppers were looking for, then broke each product, category and guide page into clear blocks that AI tools and search engines can lift as answers. It strengthened signs of expertise, such as product knowledge, origin information and real-world experience, and added a page for the brand's café.

It also reviewed the site's structured data with a plan to support FAQs and product details, linked brewing guides, blends and educational content together, and suggested ways to earn more brand mentions in forums. Custom tracking separated visits from AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini, so AI revenue could be reported for the first time.

sections.heading: The results
paragraphs: Within twelve months, AI referrals grew from a small starting point to a steady source of traffic, with a 91% engagement rate. AI-assisted conversions rose 36.5% year on year, site searches rose 182% and product quiz completions rose 247%.

Sales directly attributed to AI referrals rose 78%, and ChatGPT made up more than 95% of AI-driven transactions. AI shoppers tended to buy higher-value items such as espresso machines, gift subscriptions and brewing gear, and the brand's signature blend became the top AI-attributed product, with sales up 900% year on year.

lessons: Break pages into clear answers. The agency split product and guide pages into blocks that AI tools can quote.
Show where your products come from. Origin details and real expertise were added to build trust.
Track AI on its own. Custom tracking let the brand see AI visits, conversions and revenue apart from normal search for the first time.
caveat: This is an agency case study we rate low on trust. The brand appears only as a logo, the text says "this leading coffee brand", the 78% has no starting figure, and no one at the brand is quoted.

cardHeadline: AI shoppers spend $5.50 more per order but convert less
title: Edible: AI shoppers spend more, convert less | GEO
description: At gifting retailer Edible Brands, orders from AI shoppers are $5.50 bigger than average, but they convert below the site's usual rate.
h1: At Edible Brands, AI shoppers spend more but convert less
intro: Gifting retailer Edible Brands told Digital Commerce 360 that orders from AI visitors are $5.50 bigger than its site average. But those visitors convert at more than 5%, below the site's usual rate of more than 10%.

keyNumbers.label: higher average order value from AI traffic than the site average
conversion rate from AI traffic, below a site average of more than 10%
of AI referral traffic comes from ChatGPT (about)

sections.heading: The good part
paragraphs: Edible Brands is a large US gifting retailer, No. 182 in the Digital Commerce 360 Top 1000. Chief digital officer Erica Randerson said AI is still a small slice of its traffic, less than 10%, and ChatGPT accounts for about 95% of it.
Those shoppers spend more. The average order from AI traffic is $5.50 greater than the site average, and Randerson said AI traffic seems a little more immune to the pull of lower-priced goods.

sections.heading: The less good part
paragraphs: AI visitors convert at more than 5%, which Randerson called strong. But it is lower than Edible's site average of more than 10%. She put that high average down to the kind of store Edible is: people arrive to buy a gift, usually knowing who it is for.

quotes.text: But I will say: That's lower than our site average.
quotes.who: Erica Randerson, chief digital officer at Edible Brands

quotes.text: We have a high intent audience. They're coming in knowing who they're shopping for most of the time.
quotes.who: Erica Randerson, chief digital officer at Edible Brands

lessons: Compare AI shoppers with your own average. At Edible they looked strong on their own but converted below the site's usual rate.
Know your baseline. Edible's regular shoppers already arrive with a clear goal, which is why its normal conversion rate is so high.
Look at order value too. Even with lower conversion, Edible's AI orders were $5.50 bigger on average.
caveat: A mixed result: AI shoppers spend a little more per order but convert below the site's usual rate. Results like this vary from store to store.

source.title: How AI referrals are impacting traffic at 4 online retailers
source.author: Abbas Haleem
